approach: Add an optional `mirrored_sources` section to the job plan. One entry has `content` (what the job writes), `source` (the governing source), `places` (every place in the source the content depends on) and `comparison` (the number of the criterion whose demonstration compares the written content to every place, not only its structure). A new admission rule, `mirrored_sources_findings(mirrors, criteria)`, called from `plan_findings` after `dependents_findings`, raises one major finding per fault: a blank `content` or `source`, an empty or all-blank places list, or a `comparison` of 0 or above the criteria count. A major finding sends the plan back to the planner with no critic call, the same path as `dependents`. An empty list means the plan mirrors nothing and gives no finding. Whether a demonstration exists for the comparison criterion is NOT re-checked, since `plan_findings` already raises a major finding for any criterion without exactly one demonstration (admission.rs:188-198). The section is stored on `JobPlan` (`serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")`) and shown by `plan_body` only when non-empty, so old records and plans without mirrored content serialise and render as before. The prompts get short bullets sized against the 700-token frame limit (lib.rs:404), not only the 1300 set budget: the planner bullet is at most about 170 bytes and the critic bullet at most about 330 bytes. The full rule text goes in the `PlanMirrorOutput` field doc comments, which become schema descriptions the planner sees (the pattern of `urgent_reason`, outputs.rs:38). What a shape check cannot see (a plan that mirrors content but gives `[]`, a places list that omits a place, a comparing demonstration that checks only structure) is the critic's job and marked prose-only. The fixture is a plan whose entry names a source but lists no places: it is refused in a new corpus table, in admission unit tests, and end to end through the scripted planner; the same plan with places listed is accepted.

decisions.choice: Structured plan section with an admission shape rule, plus a critic prompt rule for what a shape check cannot see.
decisions.reason: The critic is a model, so a rejection of a plan with no list is not deterministic; a tested admission finding is. The defaults say a rule that matters is enforced by mechanism or marked prose-only, and the `dependents` section is the model: admission checks shape, the critic checks completeness against its own search.

rejected.why: A fixture cannot make a model critic reject; the rejection could not be tested and the user asked for a rejected fixture.

rejected.option: Fold the list into `dependents` through a new DependentKind variant
rejected.why: One entry per place cannot show a source with no places, and an entry has no field for the comparing criterion. The fixture would have nothing to reject.

rejected.option: Detect mirroring by keywords in the plan text or the reading's criteria (mirror, cache key, seed, definition)
rejected.why: The keywords hit unrelated plans, including this one, so the refusal rate would rise on a guess. Whether a plan mirrors a source is the planner's declaration, backed by the critic.

decisions.choice: The section is `Vec<PlanMirror>`; an empty list or a missing key means the plan mirrors nothing and gets no finding.
decisions.reason: Most plans mirror nothing. It also leaves the existing plan JSON fixtures (fake.rs:379, lifecycle.rs:2669, introspection.rs:737, run/tests.rs:794, job_plan.rs:431) valid with no edits, and old records re-serialise byte for byte.

rejected.option: Make the section required and refuse an empty list like `dependents`
rejected.why: Most plans would be refused or padded, and six JSON fixtures in non-deliverable crates would need edits.

rejected.option: Use `Option<Vec<_>>` so a missing key can be refused
rejected.why: It separates 'forgot' from '[]' but every JSON fixture would need the key. The critic prompt covers 'forgot'.

decisions.choice: The comparison is checked for shape only: the number is 1 to the criteria count. The no-demonstration case is dropped from the new rule (answers finding 10). A unit test shows a comparison that points at a criterion with no demonstration yields only the existing 'needs exactly one' finding and no mirror finding.
decisions.reason: `plan_findings` already raises a major finding for any in-range criterion without exactly one demonstration (admission.rs:188-198); a second finding for the same fault would also contradict the 'exactly one finding' claim. Whether the demonstration compares content to every place stays with the critic, since a keyword check of the demonstration text would be a guess.

rejected.option: Keep the no-demonstration check in the new rule
rejected.why: It duplicates an existing finding on the same fault.

rejected.option: Require the demonstration's `observes` to contain every place string
rejected.why: A place is often a long description, so the check would refuse good plans and pass a stuffed one.

decisions.choice: Word the rule as: the demonstration of criterion `comparison` must compare the written content against every listed place, not only its structure. If the reading has no criterion that can carry that comparison, the planner points `comparison` at the nearest one and raises a `User:` open question saying so. The wording goes in the planner bullet, the `PlanMirrorOutput.comparison` field doc and the critic bullet (answers finding 11).
decisions.reason: The planner cannot add acceptance criteria; criteria come from the accepted reading and the plan references them by number. The demonstration is the planner's lever, and the critic checks that demonstration.

rejected.option: Tell the planner to add a criterion
rejected.why: The plan has no field for criteria; admission counts the reading's criteria.

decisions.choice: Do not add a mechanical path check on `places` (finding 12 considered and declined). The field doc asks for `path:line` or `path, term` where the source is in the repository, and the critic's own Grep judges completeness; the shape rule stays as planned.
decisions.reason: `plan_findings` has only an `is_directory` callback, not a file-exists callback (admission.rs:172-177). Path existence for files comes from the `exists` flag Athena sets on planned files, not from a lookup. A prefix-must-be-a-path rule needs a new callback parameter on `plan_findings` and its callers, and would refuse a place in a brief or a request, which is not a repository file (a brief definition, a seeded record id). That risks refusing good plans for a partial gain. The mechanism catches an empty list; completeness stays prose-only, marked so in the prompts and design doc.

rejected.option: Require each place to start with a relative path and check it against the base
rejected.why: Needs a new existence callback, breaks for sources outside the repository, and still cannot tell a complete list from a partial one.

rejected.option: Check only that each place contains a path-like token (a `/` or a `.ext`)
rejected.why: A guess that refuses prose places such as 'the Definitions section of the brief' and passes a vague 'foo.rs'.

decisions.choice: Show the section in `plan_body` in briefs.rs only when non-empty, so the critic, a revision brief and the producer section see the list.
decisions.reason: The critic cannot judge a list it is not shown, and the producer needs the places to write the content from. When it is empty the rendered bytes are unchanged, so existing producer-section hashes still match.

rejected.option: Leave it out of the briefs
rejected.why: The critic would see only the approach text.

decisions.reason: It holds the queue planner for `athena plan`, not the job plan. The job-plan code is in admission.rs, run/planning.rs and records.rs. The PR note says so.

decisions.choice: Size the prompt edits against the 700-token frame limit (answers finding 9). demonstrations.observes: Each incomplete plan (no places, only blank places, blank source, comparison 0, comparison above the criteria count) produces exactly one major Athena finding at location `mirrored sources, entry 1` whose summary says the entry lists no places or names the comparison fault.
